newsitem.title: USA: Metallurg Inc and Shieldalloy exit Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Metallurg Inc and Shieldalloy exit Chapter 11.

text.p: Holding company Metallurg Inc and its main U.S. subsidiary, Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corp, completed their operational and financial restructuring to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, the company said in a statement.
Michael Banks, vice president of administration at the New York-based holding company, told Reuters that five million shares are being distributed to claim holders by the privately-held group.
But about 4.5 million shares were likely to remain with the claimants, while the balance would be thinly traded on the over-the-counter market.
All outstanding issues of debt have been resolved, Banks said.
Metallurg was founded in 1911 and employs 1,700 people worldwide, with 300 in the U.S., producing vanadium, chrome and aluminum products, three sectors which generate half of the company's revenues.
The key shareholders are Franklin Mutual, SBC Warburg, Contrarian Fund, Cerberus, and Morgan's Waterfall.
"They have all expressed their intention of being long-term investors," Banks said.
There were no immediate plans to raise cash for any expansion plans now the holding company is out of Chapter 11, Banks said.
Metallurg and Shieldalloy entered court protection in September 1993. None of Metallurg's other worldwide operations which are also part of the Metallurg Group, sought protection.
The company said it made a loss of $24.5 million in 1993, switching to an operating profit of $26.4 million in 1996, $33.0 million in 1995, and $7.4 million in 1994.
"We expect our financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 1997 also to be strong," Metallurg chairman and CEO Michael Standen said.
Stronger vanadium prices helped boost Metallurg's coffers.
Operations have been reorganised to reduce exposure to cyclical and other cahnges.

"We have expanded our sourcing from Russia and China of such materials as silicon metal, manganese metal, and silico-chrome, and developed several new products such as superfine aluminum powders, hydride alloys and metal-base chemicals," Standen said.
Unprofitable or low-margin operations such as tin production in Brazil and ferro-vanadium in Germany have been stopped.

Other highlights in the reorganisation included selling assets in the U.S., expansion of polishing powder and boron alloy output in the U.K.-based London & Scandinavian subsidiary, reorganizing Gesellshaft fur Elektrometallurgie in Germany, and setting up a subsidiary in Shanghai to improve raw materials sourcing.
The company's operations in Brazil were also reorganized to focus on aluminum master alloys and tablets, tantalum and niobium (columbium) oxides.
Last year Metallurg also bought a small stake in Solikamsk magnesium works in Russia.
